turns.text: If we take AlphaFold apart, which idea truly changed the direction of research?

DeepMind’s AlphaFold2 achieved a major jump in protein structure prediction at CASP14 by combining evolutionary information, attention-based representations, and end-to-end structure refinement. It showed how deep learning could transform a long-standing scientific problem.
That sounds like a promising direction. What mechanism actually makes it work?

Sequence and multiple-sequence alignment features flow through pair and structure modules to predict a folded 3D protein model. The system turns evolutionary constraints into coordinates that scientists can inspect and test.

Experts generally treat AlphaFold2 as a landmark in scientific machine learning because it changed what biologists could routinely look up and test. Its long-term legacy is the expectation that AI systems can act as infrastructure for discovery, not only as benchmark models.
Seen alongside AlphaGo, AlphaFold reveals how the same technical question can echo across different eras.
